questions.question: A learner builds one transform with RandomHorizontalFlip, RandomCrop, ToTensor and Normalize, and passes it to the training, validation and test datasets. What is the main problem?
options: Normalize must always come before ToTensor.
Validation and test images are randomly changed, so their scores vary between runs and no longer measure performance on real images.
Random augmentation makes training slower, so it should be used only on the test set.
RandomCrop cannot be used on greyscale images.
questions.explanation: Augmentation belongs to the training data only; evaluation data needs the same fixed preprocessing and nothing random. The most tempting wrong option is the order of Normalize and ToTensor: the order given is actually correct, because Normalize works on the tensor that ToTensor produces.

questions.question: Why does a convolutional layer need far fewer parameters than a fully connected layer on the same image?
options: Because it converts the image to greyscale before processing it.
Because pooling removes most of the weights after training.
Because it only works on small images such as 28 × 28 pixels.
Because each small filter looks at a local patch and the same weights are shared across every position in the image.
questions.explanation: Local connections and weight sharing mean a filter's few weights are reused everywhere, so the count does not grow with image size. The most tempting wrong option is pooling: pooling reduces the spatial size of feature maps and later computation, but it has no weights of its own and does not remove weights from the convolution.

questions.question: After 20 epochs, the training loss has fallen steadily, while the validation loss reached its lowest value at epoch 5 and has risen slowly since. What is the best diagnosis and first action?
options: Underfitting; make the model larger and train for more epochs.
The learning rate is too high; divide it by 10.
Overfitting; keep the epoch-5 checkpoint and add regularisation or augmentation.
The training is healthy; report the epoch-20 model.
questions.explanation: Separating curves, with validation loss rising after an early minimum, are the sign of overfitting. The most tempting wrong option is the high learning rate, but that pattern shows a loss that jumps or grows for the training data too, while here the training loss falls smoothly.

questions.question: A learner's early-stopping code saves the best model with best_state = model.state_dict() and reloads it after training stops. The reloaded model always behaves like the last epoch. Why?
options: state_dict() returns references to the live weight tensors, so best_state keeps changing as training continues; a deep copy or torch.save is needed.
Early stopping only works when dropout is removed from the model.
load_state_dict() can only load weights saved by the optimiser.
The patience value was too small, so training never stopped early.
questions.explanation: Without copy.deepcopy or torch.save, the stored dictionary points at the same tensors that the optimiser keeps updating. The most tempting wrong option is the patience value: patience decides when training stops, but it cannot explain why the saved 'best' weights are identical to the final ones.

questions.question: A learner loads a pretrained ResNet, freezes all layers, replaces model.fc, and trains the head. Later they set requires_grad = True on layer4 but keep the old optimiser, which was built with model.fc.parameters(). What happens?
options: layer4 is fine-tuned with the head's learning rate.
Training raises an error because frozen layers cannot be unfrozen.
layer4 receives gradients but is never updated, because the optimiser does not know about its parameters.
The whole network is retrained from random weights.
questions.explanation: An optimiser only updates the parameters it was given, so the optimiser must be rebuilt after changing what is trainable, ideally with a lower learning rate for layer4. The most tempting wrong option is that layer4 is fine-tuned with the head's rate; this would only be true if the optimiser had been rebuilt to include layer4.
